description: ODC (coverage T): RECORD AND LIST LITERALS, four types that no verb names because they are born from the TEXT written in an argument. In ODC an expression property is written by ExpressionDefinition.Parse: text between curly braces becomes an IRecordLiteralExpression with one IRecordLiteralField per 'Name: value' pair; text between square brackets becomes an IListLiteralExpression with one IListLiteralItem per element. It only works where the property declares SupportsRecordAndListLiterals - the Value of an IArgument, and also the Value of the field itself and of the element itself, which is why they nest. One action receives the three formats (record, list of records, list of texts) and the public action calls it passing the literals.

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio gives an error); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops._why: the argument must have a CONCRETE record type: it is from it that the literal takes the attributes to bind to each field
uses the three inputs inside the action itself: an IInputParameter unused in the body catches the warning UnusedElement

HERE is born 1 IRecordLiteralExpression + 2 IRecordLiteralField. Writing this argument with a variable name would give a normal expression; the curly braces are the only difference. The argument must be BLANK (Value null): only then does the kernel use IArgument.SetValue(ExpressionDefinition), which is what recognizes {} and []. If there is already an expression, the set goes through the expression.Text path and the same text is stored as a literal ITextBasedExpression - the second set does NOT replace one literal with another

ONE op covers the four types at once: 1 IListLiteralExpression, 2 IListLiteralItem and, because the Value of an item is also SupportsRecordAndListLiterals, 2 IRecordLiteralExpression with 2 IRecordLiteralField each. It is the dominant form in real code (list of records)
the minimal case: the items of a list of texts store an ITextBasedExpression instead of a record
the second door to the same type: instead of the text, the parent's factory (IListLiteralExpression.CreateItem). The item is born without a Value and then receives its own record literal
reads back the argument: the model recomposes the text '{ ProjectName: "Alpha", OpenTasks: 3 }' from the fields
proves the whole tree: IListLiteralExpression > 3 IListLiteralItem (2 from the text, 1 from the create) > IRecordLiteralExpression > IRecordLiteralField
proves the IListLiteralItem over plain text
